Mika uses apps on a separate virtual screen. That needs Android 12 or later; this phone runs Android %1$s. You can still use chat, web and sandbox tasks.
Turn on the accessibility service

Mika uses the accessibility service to read and control its own virtual screen. Find Mika under Accessibility in system settings (on some phones it’s under “Downloaded apps” or “Installed services”) and turn it on.
System settings show Mika’s accessibility service as on, but it isn’t actually running (this often happens after Mika is force-stopped). Turn Mika off in accessibility settings, then on again.
If Android blocks you from turning on Mika, open Mika’s app info and choose “Allow restricted settings” from the menu if that option is available. Then return to Accessibility and turn on Mika.

Android may block accessibility for apps installed outside an app store until restricted settings are allowed. Open Mika’s app info, open its menu, and choose “Allow restricted settings” if it is available. Then turn Mika off and on again under Accessibility.
Thêm mô hình
Mika needs a large language model with tool calling to think and act. Just enter the provider’s URL, the model name and an API key.
Android 14 or later recommended

On Android 12–13, background work may affect focus on your screen: when Mika opens an app or scrolls on the virtual screen, the field you’re typing in may briefly lose focus and need another tap. From Android 14 the virtual screen has its own focus. This phone runs Android %1$s; tasks still work normally.
